texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of a road accident that occurred on 10.07.2018, in which the petitioner Mukesh Kumar Pal allegedly suffered grievous injury. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 10.07.2018 at around 06:00 p.m, petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing no.DL-13SN-0538 which was driven by one Sonu. When they reached in front of Meerut Trisection Patel Nagar, Mukesh Kumar vs Gordhan Das on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3260310/ 1 suddenly a bus bearing no. UK-07PA-1374 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) hit the motorcycle. Due to this impact, petitioner suffered grievous injury. He was taken to Yashoda Hospital for treatment. 3. An FIR no.1417 of 2018 dated 11.07.2018 was registered u/s 279,338,427 of IPC at PS Sihani Gate, District Ghaziabad and the matter was investigated. After investigation, a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle (respondent no.1) while a claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver and respondent no.2 is the owner of offending vehicle. Offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident. 5. In response to the claim, respondent no.1 filed his reply denying the occurrence of the accident and refuting the allegations of rash and negligent driving on the part of driver. 6. On the basis of pleadings on record, following issues were framed on 08.04.2021. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 10.07.2018 due to rash MACT NO: 71/2020 Mukesh Kumar Pal v. Gordhan & anr. P.No 2 of 20 ss Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.05.28 16:01:15 +0530 and negligent driving of vehicle no.UK-07PA-1374 being driven by R1 and owned by R2? OPP. 3. Relief. 7. In order to prove its case, petitioner no.1 examined himself as PW-1 and Sh. Manish Gupta, employed as technician in MAX Healthcare, examined as PW-2. PW-1/Mukesh Kumar tendered his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A wherein he deposed that on 10.07.2018 at about 06:00 p.m. he along with his friend Sonu was going towards Ghaziabad from Delhi by motorcycle No.DL-13SN-0538 which was being driven by him at a normal speed. When he reached in front of Meerut Tiraha, Chowki Patel Nagar. A bus bearing no. UK-07PA-1374 came in a very high speed without blowing any horn and hit the motorcycle of PW-1. Due to this impact they fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and was taken to Yashoda Hospital, Ghaziabad. Where PW-1 hospitalized from 10.07.2018 to 11.07.2018 and then he was taken to Max Super Speciality Hospital where he was hospitalized from 11.07.2018 to 22.07.2018. He was again hospitalized from 30.09.2018 to 30.09.2018 at Krishna Hospital & trauma Center. PW-1 was duly cross examined by respondent no.2. MACT NO: 71/2020 Mukesh Kumar Pal v. Gordhan & anr. P.No 3 of 20 ss CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.05.28 16:01:19 +0530 PW-2/Manish Gupta deposed that he brought the summon record as complete medical record of Sh. Mukesh Kumar, s/o Sh. Manphool Singh, r/o H.No.25, Gali no. 32, Molar Bandh Ext. Badarpur, New Delhi. He relied upon the Authority letter issued by medical superintendent in his favour as Ex.PW2/A, identity card of PW-2 as Ex.PW2/B, medical treatment already Ex.PW1/1 and medical bills as already Ex.PW1/2. PW-2 was not cross examined by respondents. 8. No respondent evidence was led by respondents. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
texts.arguments: 12. It is a law well settled in Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. ((2009) 13 SC 530) in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, (2001 ACJ 421 SC), in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as (2009 ACJ 287), that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 18. Further it is noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the MACT NO: 71/2020 Mukesh Kumar Pal v. Gordhan & anr. P.No 6 of 20 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.05.28 16:01:32 +0530 following: Mukesh Kumar vs Gordhan Das on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3260310/ 4 Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 18.1 18.2 It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 18.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and MACT NO: 71/2020 Mukesh Kumar Pal v. Gordhan & anr. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 18.5. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. They are taking such a rigid and mechanical approach without understanding and appreciating the distinction drawn by this Court in MACT NO: 71/2020 Mukesh Kumar Pal v. Gordhan & anr.
